root_cause.text: The `ip6_datagram_send_ctl()` function in the IPv6 datagram path accumulates option lengths into 16-bit fields (`opt_flen` and `opt_nflen`) without subtracting the length of the previously stored option before adding a new one when handling repeated `IPV6_DSTOPTS`, `IPV6_HOPOPTS`, or `IPV6_RTHDR` ancillary messages, allowing integer overflow that causes a mismatch between the headroom calculation and the actual extension header push length, leading to `skb_under_panic()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch explicitly subtracts the previous option length before adding the new length, e.g., `if (opt->dst1opt) opt->opt_flen -= ipv6_optlen(opt->dst1opt);` and similar for `dst0opt` and `srcrt`. The CVE description confirms that repeated large `IPV6_DSTOPTS` messages cause `opt_flen` to wrap (32 * 2048 + 8 = 65544 → 8 as `__u16`), while `dst1opt` still points to a 2048-byte header, leading to the panic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a new pointer variable orthdr to hold original routing header in ip6_datagram_send_ctl
intent_record.what: Added a new local variable `struct ipv6_rt_hdr *orthdr` before the existing `struct ipv6_rt_hdr *rthdr` in function `ip6_datagram_send_ctl`.
intent_record.how: Introduces an uninitialized pointer variable on the stack; no change in runtime behavior until the variable is assigned or used.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix length double counting when replacing existing destination option header in IPv6 datagram control message handling.
intent_record.what: Added conditional subtraction of previous option length from opt->opt_flen and opt->opt_nflen before assigning new destination option headers
intent_record.how: When setting a new destination option header (dst1opt or dst0opt), if a previous header already existed, its length is subtracted from the corresponding total length field before adding the new length, preventing double counting when the option is replaced.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix incorrect accounting of optional header length when updating routing headers or destination options in ip6_datagram_send_ctl, ensuring opt->opt_nflen reflects the accurate total length after replacement.
intent_record.what: In the IPv6 datagram send control function, when updating the source routing header (srcrt) or destination options (dst0opt), the code now subtracts the length of the previously stored header (if any) from opt->opt_nflen before adding the new length. Specifically: for srcrt, subtract old orthdr length; for dst0opt, subtract old opt->dst0opt length.
intent_record.how: This change prevents opt->opt_nflen from being incorrectly inflated when a routing header or destination option is replaced. Previously, the old length was not removed, leading to an overcount of optional header lengths. Now the net length is correctly updated by removing the old before adding the new.

The group directly addresses the vulnerability by fixing the incorrect accounting of optional header lengths in ip6_datagram_send_ctl(), specifically preventing double counting when replacing existing options, which matches the root cause of integer overflow leading to skb_under_panic().

candidates.rationale: Adds the new destination option length to opt_flen without subtracting the length of any previously stored option, leading to integer overflow when the same option type is set repeatedly.
Adds the new hop-by-hop option length to opt_nflen without subtracting the length of any previously stored option, causing double count and eventual overflow.
Adds the new routing header length to opt_nflen without subtracting the length of a previously stored routing header, leading to integer overflow.
When a 2292 routing header replaces a destination option, adds the destination option header length to opt_nflen without subtracting the previous routing header length, contributing to overflow.

vuln_statements.explanation: Adds new destination option length to opt_flen without subtracting the length of any previously stored destination option. When the same IPV6_DSTOPTS ancillary message is sent repeatedly, this causes double counting and eventual integer overflow, leading to headroom mismatch and skb_under_panic.

Adds new hop-by-hop option length to opt_nflen without subtracting the length of any previously stored hop-by-hop option. When the same IPV6_HOPOPTS ancillary message is sent repeatedly, this causes double counting and eventual integer overflow, leading to headroom mismatch and skb_under_panic.

Adds new routing header length to opt_nflen without subtracting the length of any previously stored routing header (IPV6_RTHDR). When the same routing header ancillary message is sent repeatedly, this causes double counting and eventual integer overflow, leading to headroom mismatch and skb_under_panic.

When a 2292 routing header replaces a destination option, adds the destination option header length to opt_nflen without subtracting the previous routing header length. This contributes to cumulative length accounting error, leading to integer overflow and subsequent skb_under_panic.
